nm_barn_yard_the.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone boulders on the edge of Gallup, tucked beneath the red ridge of the Gallup Hogback. All 23 problems are bouldering, mostly in the easy to moderate range (roughly V1 to V3), with a few harder lines stretching up to about V6. Most established problems are solid, but some of the stone is sandy and crumbly, so test holds before pulling hard. The boulders sit only a couple of minutes from where you leave the car, which makes this a quick, quiet session spot that climbers have been enjoying since the late 1990s.

nm_winter_wall_2.blurb: A tall wall in Diablo Canyon, in the high desert west of Santa Fe, and the first cliff you see on reaching the parking area. It holds 23 mostly sport routes plus some trad, with grades from 5.7 to 5.12 and a big cluster in the 5.10s. Many pitches run well beyond 100 feet, so bring a long rope or plan on rappelling in stages. The wall gets plenty of sun, which makes it the canyon's best choice in cooler months. Some of the rock is chossy, so a helmet is wise for both climber and belayer.

nm_north_cliffband.blurb: A band of short cliffs on Cochiti Mesa, in the Jemez country between Albuquerque and Santa Fe, lying northwest of the downclimb. The 23 listed routes are mostly sport with some trad and top-rope setups, spanning 5.6 to 5.13 with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. It was long regarded as the handiest crag on the mesa, with trees for shade and a lively crowd at its base. The 2011 Las Conchas fire scorched the mesa, so rock quality and old hardware may have suffered; look for recent reports before planning a trip.

nm_campground.blurb: A small crag at the Forest Service campground in Luna Park, in the hills northeast of Monticello within the Truth or Consequences region. Of 23 climbs, most are bolted sport routes, with a few trad lines, some top-rope options and a single boulder problem. Grades run mostly from the easiest 5.x climbs to around 5.10, so it suits climbers building mileage on moderate lines. The rock is volcanic and of middling quality. Several routes begin steps from where you stop the car, and camping is right beside the cliff.
nm_campground.parking_note: Drive up to the small Forest Service campground at Luna Park; the routes start right beside the camping area, within a few steps of where you stop.
nm_campground.approach: Essentially none: park at the campground and walk about ten yards to the base of the routes.

nm_runway_lower_tier.blurb: The lowest tier of the Early Wall in Diablo Canyon near Santa Fe, home to the longest single-pitch lines on this side of the canyon. All 23 routes are sport, running from one easy 5.8 up to 5.12, with 5.11 the most common grade and a good number of 5.10s. Expect sustained, tenuous face and slab climbing with several cruxes, a good training ground for experienced sport climbers. The wall catches only an hour or two of early sun, which makes it a pleasant place to be in hot weather.
nm_runway_lower_tier.approach: Follow the trail that leaves the arroyo opposite the start of the Winter Wall path and contours west to the base of the cliff.

nm_red_wall.blurb: The tallest cliff at the Box near Socorro, standing about 170 feet on the east side of Box Canyon. Its 22 routes split between sport and trad, with grades from 5.7 to 5.12 and a spread of 5.8s through 5.11s. The rhyolite looks shaky at first glance but proves quite solid. It faces southwest and takes sun from late morning through the afternoon. Many routes stop partway up, and a few continue to the top. The wall sees fewer visitors than neighboring cliffs, and many older lines need gear in addition to their bolts.

nm_minor_wall.blurb: A short, quirky wall in the Box climbing area near Socorro, mixing sport, trad and a bit of bouldering across 22 climbs. Most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.11, with a few easier lines and some harder ones. Lines are brief, around 25 feet, and the climbing is technical and sequential with plenty of hidden holds, making it a decent onsight test for climbers around 5.11. The rock is sharp. The faces point in several directions, mostly south and west, and shade makes summer visits comfortable. Climbing is possible all year.
